title: Kamada Reports Record-High First Nine Months 2026 Financial Results; Increases 2026 Annual Guidance and Projects Double-Digit Growth in Revenues and Profitability in 2027
summary: Record-Breaking Nine-Month Results: Record High Nine-Month Revenues of $152.2 Million, up 12% Year-over-Year; and Record High Nine-Month Adjusted EBITDA of $40.9 Million, a 27% Margin of Revenues, up 20% Year-over-Year Strong Third Quarter Performance: Revenues of $52.0 Million, up 11% Year-over-Year; Third Quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $15.2 Million, a 29% Margin of Revenues, up 30% […]
body_markdown:
- ***R*** ***ecord-Breaking*** ***Nine-Month Results:*** *Record High Nine-Month Revenues of $152.2 Million, up 12% Year-over-Year; and Record High Nine-Month Adjusted EBITDA of $40.9 Million, a 27% Margin of Revenues, up 20% Year-over-Year*
- ***Strong Third Quarter Performance:*** *Revenues of $52.0 Million, up 11% Year-over-Year; Third Quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $15.2 Million, a 29% Margin of Revenues, up 30% Year-over-Year*
- ***Accelerating Bottom-Line Growth:*** *Third Quarter Net Income of $8.0 Million, up 51% Year-over-Year; Net Income for the First Nine Months of $21.4 Million, up 29% Year-over-Year*
- ***Raises 2026 Full–Year Guidance:*** *Revenue Guidance Increased to $205 Million – $208 Million and Adjusted EBITDA Guidance to $52 Million – $54 Million, Representing Annual Double-Digit Organic Profitable Growth*
- ***Strong Growth Momentum Extending into 2027:*** *Kamada Projects Double-Digit Growth in Both Revenues and Profitability in 202* *7* *; Detailed Guidance to be* *Provided in January 202* *7*
- ***Robust Cash Generation*** ***:*** *Cash Flow from Operating Activities Reaches $37.6 Million in the First Nine Months of 2026; Strong Cash Balance of $75.3 Million at the End of the Third Quarter*
- ***Driving Inorganic Growth*** ***:*** *Company Remains Focused on Accelerating Growth Through Business Development and M&A Transactions*
- ***D*** ***ividend Distribution:*** *Declares Cash Dividend of $0.14 Per Share* *(Approximately $8.0 Million); Together with Dividend Payments Made Earlier this Year Amount to $0.56 per share (Approximately $32.2 Million) for the Year*
- *Conference Call and Live Webcast Today at 8:30am ET*


**REHOVOT, Israel, and HOBOKEN, NJ – November 9, 2026** — Kamada Ltd. (NASDAQ: KMDA; TASE: KMDA.TA), a global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived therapies field, today announced financial results for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of its 2026 annual guidance, and a dividend payment.


“During the third quarter of 2026, we continued the strong operational and financial performance we have demonstrated throughout the year, with double-digit growth in revenues and adjusted EBITDA resulting in record high results for the first nine months of 2026,” said Amir London, Kamada’s Chief Executive Officer. “The underlying demand for our products, especially KEDRAB® in the U.S. market, as well as VARIZIG® and HEPAGAM®, continues to expand. Based on our excellent performance, we are increasing our 2026 annual guidance to a range of $205 million to $208 million of revenues and $52 million to $54 million of adjusted EBITDA, with the mid-points representing 14% and 26% growth, respectively, compared to 2025 results. Our strong growth momentum is expected to continue into 2027 with a projection of double-digit growth in both revenues and profitability.”
“We continue to ramp up plasma collection at our Texas-based facilities in support of our new three-year, approximately $50 million supply agreement. We also remain committed to expanding our current commercial portfolio through business development and M&A opportunities to further accelerate our organic growth. Lastly, we are pleased to announce another cash dividend of $0.14 per share for a total payment of approximately $8.0 million to be paid to our shareholders during the fourth quarter, which together with dividend payments made earlier this year amount to $32.2 million for the year. Our ability to continue paying dividends while continuing to invest in our commercial growth is indicative of our excellent financial and operational strength,” concluded Mr. London.


Click[here](https://www.kamada.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026-11-09-KMDA-Q3-2026-Results-only.pdf) to review the full financial report.


**Financial Highlights for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026**


- Total revenues were $52.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, up 11% compared to $47.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in revenues was driven by the diversity of the Company’s portfolio, primarily attributable to increased sales of KEDRAB in the U.S. market, as well as VARIZIG and HEPAGAM sales.
- Gross profit and gross margins were $23.3 million and 45%, respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to $19.8 million and 42%, respectively, in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in gross profit and gross margin was primarily attributable to higher gross margins of the Company’s proprietary products, due to improved product and markets sales mix.
- Operating expenses, including R&D, S&M, G&A and other expenses, totaled $13.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to $11.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher G&A and S&M expenses in support of our increased commercial operations.
- Net income was $8.0 million, or $0.14 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2026, up 51% compared to $5.3 million, or $0.09 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025.
- Adjusted EBITDA, as detailed in the tables below, was $15.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 30% compared to $11.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter represents a 29% margin of revenues and is the outcome of the Company’s continued commercial growth.


- Cash provided by operating activities was $19.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to $10.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in operating cash flow is indicative of the Company’s ability to convert its increased profitability into cash flow.


**Financial Highlights for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026**


- Total revenues for the first nine months of 2026 were a record $152.2 million, a 12% increase from $135.8 million generated in the first nine months of 2025. The increase in revenues was driven by the diversity of the Company’s portfolio, primarily attributable to increased sales of KEDRAB in the U.S. market, as well as growth in the Distribution segment, where revenues increased year-over-year by 35% to $24.1 million.
- Gross profit and gross margins for the first nine months of 2026 were $64.9 million and 43%, respectively, compared to $59.4 million and 44%, respectively, in the first nine months of 2025. The increase in gross profit was driven by the increase in total revenues.
- Operating expenses, including R&D, S&M, G&A and other expenses, totaled $38.1 million for the first nine months of 2026, as compared to $36.8 million in the first nine months of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher G&A and S&M expenses in support of the Company’s expanded commercial operations.
- Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was $21.4 million, or $0.37 per diluted share, up 29% as compared to $16.6 million, or $0.29 per diluted share, in the first nine months of 2025.
- Adjusted EBITDA, as detailed in the tables below, was a record $40.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, a 20% increase as compared to $34.2 million in the first nine months of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months represents a 27% margin of revenues and is the outcome of the Company’s continued commercial growth.
- Cash provided by operating activities during the first nine months of 2026 was approximately $37.6 million, as compared to $17.9 million during the first nine months of 2025. The increase in operating cash flow is indicative of the Company’s ability to convert its increased profitability into cash flow.


**Balance Sheet Highlights** As of September 30, 2026, Kamada had cash, cash equivalents and short-term investment totaling $75.3 million, as compared to $75.5 million as of December 31, 2025. During the third quarter, the Company executed a $9.8 million dividend payment, bringing total dividends already paid in 2026 to $24.2 million. The Company’s ability to maintain its strong cash position while making these dividend payments is another indication of its ability to convert its increased profitability into cash flow.


**** **Recent Corporate Highlights**


- Declared cash dividend of $0.14 per share, totaling approximately $8.0 million. Total dividend payments already made in 2026 prior to the current payment were $0.42 per share, totaling approximately $24.2 million.
- Announced the expansion of its biosimilar portfolio with the commercial launch of two additional new products in Israel, adding to its existing portfolio of two products. Kamada expects its growing biosimilar product portfolio to generate approximately $10 million in annual revenue in 2028 and approximately $20-$25 million in annual revenue by 2030. The Company expects the commercial availability of at least two additional biosimilar products during 2027.
- Confirmed that Kamada maintains sufficient KEDRAB supply and manufacturing capacity to meet increased demand for the product in the United States in response to a Health Advisory published by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). KEDRAB is one of only two FDA-approved anti-rabies immunoglobulin products in the U.S.
- Continued to ramp up plasma collection at its Texas-based facilities in support of its three-year, approximately $50 million agreement to supply plasma to a leading biopharmaceutical company focused on plasma-derived therapies.


**Fiscal 2026 Guidance** Kamada is increasing its 2026 annual financial guidance to total revenues in the range of $205 million to $208 million and adjusted EBITDA in the range of $52 million to $54 million, with the mid-points representing year-over-year increases of 14% in revenues and 26% in adjusted EBITDA. Prior 2026 annual guidance was total revenues in the range of $200 million to $205 million and adjusted EBITDA in the range of $50 million to $53 million.

**Non-IFRS financial measures** We present EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA because we use these non-IFRS financial measures to assess our operational performance, for financial and operational decision-making, and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons on a consistent basis. Management believes these non-IFRS financial measures are useful to investors because: (1) they allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and provide investors with a meaningful perspective on the current underlying performance of the Company’s core ongoing operations; and (2) they exclude the impact of certain items that are not directly attributable to our core operating performance and that may obscure trends in the core operating performance of the business. Non-IFRS financial measures have limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, our IFRS results. We expect to continue reporting non-IFRS financial measures, adjusting for the items described below, and we expect to continue to incur expenses similar to certain of the non-cash, non-IFRS adjustments described below. Accordingly, unless otherwise stated, the exclusion of these and other similar items in the presentation of non-IFRS financial measures should not be construed as an inference that these items are unusual, infrequent or non-recurring. EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA are not recognized terms under IFRS and do not purport to be an alternative to IFRS terms as an indicator of operating performance or any other IFRS measure. Moreover, because not all companies use identical measures and calculations, the presentation of EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. EBITDA is defined as net income (loss), plus income tax expense, plus or minus financial income or expenses, net, plus or minus income or expense in respect of securities measured at fair value, net, plus or minus income or expenses in respect of currency exchange differences and derivatives instruments, net, plus depreciation and amortization expense, whereas adjusted EBITDA is the EBITDA plus non-cash share-based compensation expenses and certain other costs.


For the projected 2026 adjusted EBITDA information presented herein, the Company is unable to provide a reconciliation of this forward measure to the most comparable IFRS financial measure because the information for these measures is dependent on future events, many of which are outside of the Company’s control. Additionally, estimating such forward-looking measures and providing a meaningful reconciliation consistent with the Company’s accounting policies for future periods is meaningfully difficult and requires a level of precision that is unavailable for these future periods and cannot be accomplished without unreasonable effort. Forward-looking non-IFRS measures are estimated in a manner consistent with the relevant definitions and assumptions noted in the Company’s adjusted EBITDA for historical periods.


**About Kamada** Kamada Ltd. (the “Company”) is a global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived therapies field. FIMI Opportunity Funds, the leading private equity firm in Israel, is the Company’s controlling shareholder, beneficially owning approximately 38% of the outstanding ordinary shares. The Company’s strategy is focused on driving profitable growth through four primary growth pillars: First, organic growth of its commercial portfolio, including continued investment in the commercialization and life cycle management of its proprietary products, consisting of six FDA-approved specialty plasma-derived products: KEDRAB®, GLASSIA®, CYTOGAM®, VARIZIG®, WINRHO SDF® and HEPAGAM B®, as well as KAMRAB®, and two equine-based anti-snake venom products. Second, distribution of third parties’ pharmaceutical products in Israel & the MENA region through in-licensing partnerships, including the launch of several biosimilar products in Israel. Third, the Company is ramping up its plasma collection operations to support revenue growth through the sale of normal source plasma to other plasma-derived manufacturers, and to support its increasing demand for hyper-immune plasma. The Company currently owns three FDA approved operating plasma collection centers in the United States, in Beaumont, Houston, and San Antonio, Texas. Fourth, the Company aims to secure new mergers and acquisitions, business development, in-licensing and/or collaboration opportunities, which are anticipated to enhance the Company’s marketed products portfolio and leverage its financial strength and existing commercial infrastructure to drive long-term profitable growth. The Company is leveraging its manufacturing, research and development expertise to advance the development and commercialization of additional product candidates, targeting areas of significant unmet medical need.
